title: End of the Road Celebrates 20 Years with Rock and Pop Festival
seoTitle: End of the Road Festival: 20 Years of Rock and Pop
subtitle: The Wiltshire festival brings together artists of all genres in celebration of its anniversary
excerpt: The 20-year-old End of the Road festival drew crowds to Larmer Tree Gardens, featuring performances by artists like Geese, Pulp, and CMAT.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The 20-year-old End of the Road festival drew crowds to Larmer Tree Gardens, where artists like Geese, Pulp, and CMAT delivered performances blending pop, rock, and experimentation. The celebration was marked by moments of nostalgia, hiatus announcements, and emotional farewells, reflecting the festival's evolution over two decades.

Anniversary Celebration with Themed Decor

During the anniversary party, the piano stage was transformed into a giant birthday cake, complete with candles and a man dressed as a toilet to mark the 'porcelain' anniversary. Jarvis Cocker led a lively singalong of Happy Birthday, wishing the festival another 20 years.

Expansion of Musical Genres Over the Years

The festival began with a focus on alt-folk and Americana, but today it hosts a variety of styles, from fun pop to experimental sound, maintaining a balance between the familiar and the unknown. The audience recalled Geese's presence, which drew a record-breaking crowd to their Thursday performance.

Memorable Performances by Iconic Artists

Pulp concluded their participation by announcing a break, performing deep cuts and B-sides, including a live debut of Deep Fried in Kelvin. CMAT announced she would not be playing in the UK for the next two years, ending her set topless, creating a moment of collective catharsis.

Diversity of Supporting Artists

In addition to the headliners, the festival featured performances by Factory Floor, Another Country $$$, Cleo Reed, James K, Model/Actriz, among others, showcasing a musical panorama ranging from industrial techno to queer country-soul. All these artists were enthusiastically received, demonstrating the audience's appetite for variety.

Cultural Importance of the Independent Festival

With a capacity of 15,000 people, End of the Road stands out by not relying on major corporate sponsors, maintaining an independent identity that contrasts with festivals receiving large corporate investments. The 20-year celebration reinforces the festival's success as a cultural landmark in the independent music scene.

With information from The Guardian, inkl, UNCUT.
